podcast.body: This song was originally hated by Rivers Cuomo, who thought it was "cheesy" and had written it on June 25, 1993, as a goofy new wave type song using a small synthesizer. The chorus came to him while walking on a college campus, and the subject was making fun of his friend, Cuyen Hee, who disliked the band making fun of his girlfriend. Despite Rivers' initial aversion, the rest of the band and producer Ric Ocasek loved it, leading to studio notes reading "we want Buddy Holly," and it eventually became the most performed song in Weezer's history, known for its legendary Happy Days-themed video directed by Spike Jonze. "Rivers had written it on June 25, 1993."

podcast.body: This song, released as a single from Weezer's 1994 debut album, was written by Rivers Cuomo out of anger because other band members were making fun of his Korean friend, King He, whom he felt protective of due to past bullying. Cuomo stated the song was about his platonic commitment to her, their relationship, and his willingness to defend her. Initially deemed "too cheesy" and an "outlier" by Cuomo, it was eventually included on the album after strong encouragement from producer Ric Ocasek and the band, with lyrics evolving from Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire to Mary Tyler Moore and Buddy Holly, and rap slang removed, with the tempo increased during production. "It's about my commitment to her, our relationship, and my willingness to defend her. It's very platonic, not a romantic thing at all."
